- Fix the root cause; do not skip tests or add workarounds.

In this repo, slug.py's slugify fails on punctuation, repeated spaces, and leading/trailing whitespace. It should produce lowercase hyphen-separated slugs with no empty segments. Run 'python3 test_slug.py', fix slugify, and verify TEST PASSED. Keep going until it passes, then report.

The current `slugify` function in `slug.py` only replaces spaces with hyphens and converts to lowercase, which does not handle punctuation, repeated spaces, or leading/trailing whitespace properly. I will fix the function to:

1. Convert to lowercase.
2. Remove leading/trailing whitespace.
3. Replace all non-alphanumeric characters with hyphens.
4. Replace repeated hyphens with a single hyphen.
5. Remove empty segments (e.g., hyphens that result from consecutive non-alphanumeric characters).

I'll update the `slug.py` file and verify the fix with the test script.

<tool_call>
{"name": "bash", "arguments": {"command": "echo 'def slugify(title):\n    return title.lower().replace(\" \", \"-\")' > slug.py"}}
</tool_call>

<tool_call>
{"name": "bash", "arguments": {"command": "echo 'def slugify(title):
    import re
    title = title.lower().strip()
    # Replace non-alphanumeric characters with hyphens
    title = re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '-', title)
    # Replace multiple hyphens with a single hyphen
    title = re.sub(r'-+', '-', title)
    # Remove empty segments (hyphens at start/end or consecutive)
    title = re.sub(r'^-+|-+$', '', title)
    return title' > slug.py"}}
